title: Bot is firing momentum/trend signals and entering trend trades, not mean reversion
analysis: Of the 50 journal entries, only 2 resulted in SUBMITTED orders — AMD (2026-05-20) and QQQ (2026-05-22). Both entries fired exclusively momentum/trend signals: 'RSI>65 (strong momentum)', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)', and '20DayHighBreakout'. These are the OPPOSITE of mean reversion signals. The bot's own CLAUDE.md Rule #6 states 'If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals,' yet QQQ was entered with ADX>25 trending confirmed. The 4 META rejections all fired legitimate mean reversion signals (RSI<45, BelowMA20>1%, ADX<25) with R:R of 3.10–3.36, but were blocked only due to existing position. Zero mean reversion entries were actually executed in this 50-entry window.
rationale: The signal scoring system currently awards points to momentum signals (RSI>65, AboveMA20>1%, ADX>25) that have no place in a mean reversion bot. These signals are accumulating enough points to cross the 2-signal threshold and trigger entries that directly contradict the stated strategy. Meanwhile, the only valid mean reversion opportunities (META) were blocked by position rules. The scoring table must be purged of momentum signals entirely.

insight.why_now: Both executed trades in this 30-day window used exclusively anti-strategy momentum signals. The bot is not functioning as a mean reversion system — it is entering trend-following trades while blocking or missing every mean reversion setup observed.
insight.purpose: Remove momentum/trend signals from the scoring table so they cannot accumulate points and trigger entries. Only signals that confirm oversold/mean-reversion conditions should score positive points.
insight.expected_effect: Eliminates trend-chasing entries entirely. Forces the bot to wait for genuine oversold conditions. Will reduce trade frequency in the short term but align every entry with the stated strategy.
insight.risks: Trade frequency may drop further until true mean reversion setups appear. If the market remains in a strong uptrend, the bot may go dormant for extended periods — which is the correct behavior for a mean reversion system in a trending regime.

current_rule:
## SIGNAL SCORING (need 2+ to enter under medium_safety profile)
- RSI < 35: +2 points (strong oversold)
- RSI < 45: +1 point (mild oversold)
- Price below lower Bollinger Band: +1 point
- Price below MA20 by > 1%: +1 point
- ADX < 25 (ranging market): +1 point (regime confirmation)
proposed_rule:
## SIGNAL SCORING (need 2+ to enter under medium_safety profile)
- RSI < 35: +2 points (strong oversold)
- RSI < 45: +1 point (mild oversold)
- Price below lower Bollinger Band: +2 points (primary mean reversion trigger)
- Price below MA20 by > 1%: +1 point
- ADX < 25 (ranging market): +1 point (regime confirmation)

NOTE: Momentum signals (RSI>65, AboveMA20>1%, ADX>25 trending, 20DayHighBreakout, PositiveSentiment) award ZERO points toward entry scoring. Their presence in signals_fired must NOT contribute to signal_score. If only momentum signals fire, action must be SKIP regardless of score.

title: 48 of 50 cycles produced no actionable mean reversion signal — scanner universe too narrow
analysis: 96% of all journal cycles in this 30-day window resulted in SKIP or REJECTED status. Of the 4 REJECTED entries (all META, all with valid mean reversion signal scores of 4 and R:R of 3.10–3.36), 100% were blocked solely because the bot already held META shares — not due to signal quality. The 2 SUBMITTED orders used momentum signals and should not have been entered. This means zero valid mean reversion trades were executed in 30 days across ~50 scanning cycles. The account held 3–4 open positions throughout (AAPL, META, AMD, QQQ visible) but the scanner apparently only evaluated these same held symbols repeatedly rather than finding new setups in a broader universe.
rationale: The bot is repeatedly re-evaluating symbols it already holds, generating rejected signals rather than scanning a broader universe for fresh mean reversion setups. With 3–4 positions permanently occupied and the scanner circling back to the same names, the bot is effectively locked out of new entries. Adding a rule to exclude currently-held symbols from the scan queue, combined with expanding the watchlist, would allow the remaining 1–2 open position slots to be filled with genuine new setups.

insight.why_now: META generated 4 valid mean reversion signals with R:R above 3.0 on May 19th, all blocked by the existing-position rule. If the scanner had pivoted to a different oversold symbol in the same time window, those 4 cycles could have produced actionable entries. The opportunity cost is directly measurable.
insight.purpose: Prevent the scanner from wasting cycles re-evaluating held positions. Redirect those cycles toward finding new mean reversion candidates in a broader watchlist. This addresses the root cause of the 96% skip rate.
insight.expected_effect: Should increase actionable signal frequency from near-zero to a more reasonable 2–5 valid setups per week. Will not degrade entry quality since signal scoring rules remain unchanged.
insight.risks: A broader universe increases exposure to lower-liquidity names. Should be limited to liquid large-caps and major ETFs (e.g., S&P 500 components, sector ETFs) to maintain execution quality. Over-expanding the universe could flood the bot with marginal setups.

current_rule: MAX OPEN POSITIONS: Never hold more than 5 positions simultaneously (medium_safety).
proposed_rule: MAX OPEN POSITIONS: Never hold more than 5 positions simultaneously (medium_safety). SCANNER RULE: Exclude all currently-held symbols from the entry scan. Do not re-evaluate a symbol for a new entry while a position in that symbol is open. Scan a minimum watchlist of 20 liquid symbols (large-cap stocks + major ETFs) each cycle to ensure sufficient opportunity set when position slots are available.

title: ADX trend filter threshold inconsistent — Rule #6 says >30 but signals fire at >25
analysis: CLAUDE.md Rule #6 states 'If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.' However, the signal scoring table awards +1 point for 'ADX < 25 (ranging market)' — creating a gap zone between ADX 25–30 where neither the trend filter blocks entry nor the ranging confirmation fires. Both executed trades (AMD, QQQ) show 'ADX>25 (trending)' in signals_fired, meaning ADX was confirmed above 25 but the Rule #6 block at >30 did not trigger. The QQQ trade entered at ADX>25 trending with a momentum breakout signal — a scenario the strategy should never permit. The 4 META rejections (the only valid mean reversion signals observed) all fired 'ADX<25 (ranging market)', confirming they were in the correct regime for mean reversion.
rationale: Tightening the ADX trend filter from >30 to >25 closes the gap zone and aligns Rule #6 with the signal scoring table. This would have blocked both executed trend-chasing trades (AMD entry at ADX>25, QQQ entry at ADX>25) while preserving the META setups which correctly showed ADX<25. The gap between the filter (30) and the scoring threshold (25) is creating a regime ambiguity that the bot is exploiting to enter trend trades.

insight.why_now: Both actual trade entries in this dataset occurred in the ADX 25–30 gap zone, indicating the inconsistency is not theoretical — it is directly causing bad entries. The filter and the scoring threshold must match.
insight.purpose: Eliminate the ambiguous ADX 25–30 zone. Any ADX reading above 25 should be treated as a trending regime and block mean reversion entries entirely.
insight.expected_effect: Would have blocked both executed trades in this window. Reduces false entries in early-trend conditions. Slightly reduces opportunity but dramatically improves entry quality alignment with strategy.
insight.risks: ADX oscillates frequently around the 25 level, so this may cause occasional whipsawing near the threshold. Consider requiring ADX > 25 for 2 consecutive bars before blocking to avoid single-bar false triggers.

current_rule: TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.
proposed_rule: TREND FILTER: If ADX > 25, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals. This threshold must match the signal scoring table's ADX < 25 ranging confirmation. There is no gap zone — ADX ≥ 25 blocks all new mean reversion entries.
